chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Ali narrated from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I heard him saying: It may be that thirty years remain for a man to live, but he regularly keeps ties with his close kinsfolk and with his near relatives, so Allah increases it to thirty-three years. And it may be that thirty-three years remain of his life, but he is undutiful towards his close kinsfolk and cuts off ties with his near relatives, so Allah reduces it to thirty years.
ai.seo_question: How does maintaining family ties affect a person's lifespan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd* illustrates the metaphysical impact of *silat al-rahim* (maintaining kinship ties) on one's *ajal* (appointed lifespan), a concept central to Shia eschatology and daily piety. The Imam specifies that filial duty and kinship can extend life by three years, whereas severing ties or being ungrateful (*'aq*) reduces it, highlighting that spiritual conduct directly influences physical longevity. This serves as a practical reminder for believers to prioritize family bonds as a means of divine blessing and extended life.
